about: Real supply-chain incidents (the exact versions that shipped malicious code) and clean controls. Each case is scanned as its own one-package project. `expect` is what a correct tool should say: compromised for an incident, not compromised for a control.

cases.name: flatmap-stream
cases.what: Maintainer handed event-stream to a stranger, who added flatmap-stream to steal Copay bitcoin wallets.

cases.name: event-stream
cases.what: The event-stream release that pulled in flatmap-stream.

cases.name: ua-parser-js
cases.what: Hijacked npm account published a cryptominer and password stealer.

cases.name: coa
cases.what: Hijacked account, same malware family as ua-parser-js.

cases.name: rc
cases.what: Hijacked account, released hours after coa.

cases.name: colors
cases.what: The author sabotaged his own package with an infinite loop (protestware).

cases.name: node-ipc
cases.what: Protestware that overwrote files on machines with Russian or Belarusian IP addresses.

cases.name: @lottiefiles/lottie-player
cases.what: Stolen publish token; the release prompted visitors to connect crypto wallets and drained them.

cases.name: @solana/web3.js
cases.what: Phished maintainer; the release exfiltrated private keys.

cases.name: ultralytics
cases.what: GitHub Actions cache poisoning shipped a cryptominer to PyPI.

cases.name: eslint-config-prettier
cases.what: Phished maintainer; install script dropped the Scavenger loader on Windows.

cases.name: is
cases.what: Same phishing campaign as eslint-config-prettier.

cases.name: num2words
cases.what: PyPI release from the same Scavenger campaign.

cases.name: nx
cases.what: s1ngularity: a postinstall script used local AI coding CLIs to hunt for secrets and published them to GitHub.

cases.name: chalk
cases.what: Phished maintainer (qix); browser crypto-clipper in 18 packages with billions of weekly downloads.

cases.name: debug
cases.what: Same campaign as chalk.

cases.name: @ctrl/tinycolor
cases.what: Shai-Hulud: a self-replicating worm that stole npm tokens and republished every package the victim maintained.

cases.name: litellm
cases.what: A credential stealer that ran on every Python startup through a .pth file.

cases.name: @tanstack/react-router
cases.what: 84 malicious versions published in six minutes with a hijacked trusted-publishing token.

cases.what: The clean release that replaced chalk 5.6.1.

cases.what: The release before the compromise.
